scenario: User clicks Visual Analyzer 'Extract Theme' but the CDP_EXTRACT channel has no main-process handler registered. The channel VISUAL_ANALYSIS_CDP_EXTRACT is defined in ipc-channels.ts but registerVisualAnalyzerIpc() never calls ipcMain.handle for it. The renderer invoke hangs for ~30s until Electron's 'No handler registered' timeout.
missingStates: CDP_EXTRACT (live token extraction from running agent via CDP)
userImpact: Visual Analyzer's core CDP extraction flow is completely non-functional. User sees a hang and opaque timeout instead of a clear 'not implemented' message. The entire Scanner->Palette->Theme pipeline cannot start from a live agent.

scenario: User initiates a Visual Analysis extraction but receives NO progress events on VISUAL_ANALYSIS_STATUS. The channel is correctly declared SEND_ONLY and no ipcMain.handle is registered, but the main process never calls webContents.send(VISUAL_ANALYSIS_STATUS, ...) anywhere. The comment in visual-analyzer-ipc.ts describes the intended push pattern but nothing implements it.
userImpact: During a long-running extraction, the UI shows an indeterminate spinner with no step-level feedback. User cannot tell if the process is working or stalled, violating the progress-must-hook-to-real-cost principle.

scenario: User's status refresh fails (e.g., IPC timeout, agent crashed) and statusStore.error is set, but the persistent StatusBar component never subscribes to the error slice. The error is consumed only inside UnifiedWorkspacePage->EnvironmentGrid (route-scoped). On any other page the error is invisible until the user navigates back to Workspace.
userImpact: A global error state lives in a global store but has no global UI surface. Users on non-Workspace pages get no indication that agent detection is failing.

scenario: User enables a per-agent wallpaper with pywal-style companion (setAndApplyAgentWallpaper). The wallpaper injects successfully, then the companion flow extracts a theme from the wallpaper and applies it. If the theme apply returns false, no notification is shown and the re-apply of wallpaper is skipped. The theme-apply-flow may have already modified agent CSS, hiding the just-injected wallpaper.
missingStates: companion_failure_recovery (notify + re-apply wallpaper when theme half fails)
userImpact: Wallpaper silently disappears after companion theme apply failure. User sees no error message and must manually re-apply the wallpaper. The apply-wallpaper action reported success even though the end state differs from what was requested.

scenario: User applies a per-agent wallpaper. The preference is persisted first (setAgentWallpaper), then injection is attempted (applyAgentWallpaper). If injection fails, the function returns {ok:false} but the preference was already persisted with enabled:true. The UI shows the wallpaper as active for that agent even though nothing was injected.
missingStates: rollback_preference_on_inject_failure (revert persisted state when injection fails)
userImpact: Preference state and runtime state diverge. After a failed inject, the UI checkbox shows enabled but no wallpaper is visible. User must toggle off/on to retry with no guidance on why it silently failed.

scenario: User clicks 'Apply to all agents' in the detail panel. The runAll function fires up to 6 concurrent apply workers, but run() only adds to pendingApps on start and removes on finish. The display shows pendingApps.size/eligibleApps.length which counts how many have STARTED, not completed. All 6 show as pending within milliseconds while actual applies take seconds.
userImpact: The 'Apply to all' progress indicator is misleading - it immediately shows 6/6 started and only drops to 0/6 when ALL complete. User has no visibility into which agents succeeded or failed until the entire batch finishes.

scenario: User creates a new environment preset with 'Apply Now'. createEnvironment calls applyToApp for the theme, then calls api.applyWallpaperToAgent(wallpaperId, agentId). If the wallpaper apply fails (wp.ok === false), the result is silently ignored - no error check, no notification.
userImpact: Environment creation reports success even though the wallpaper half failed. The user sees the new environment card but the wallpaper is not applied. No notification surfaces the partial failure.

scenario: User rapidly switches between environments. The epoch guard prevents stale completion, but each switchEnvironment call auto-creates a preset and persists via savePresets. Two rapid switches can both try to create presets for the same agent+theme combo before either completes, leading to duplicate presets on disk.
missingStates: in-flight-create deduplication (prevent duplicate presets during rapid switches)
userImpact: Rapid environment switching creates duplicate presets on disk. After restart, the user sees multiple identical presets and must manually clean them up.

scenario: User switches environments with a wallpaper bound. The epoch guard prevents the old switch from clearing dialog prompts when superseded, but does NOT abort the in-flight wallpaper IPC call (applyWallpaperToAgent / removeWallpaperFromAgent). The old operation runs to completion, racing with the new switch's operations.
supportedStates: epoch guard (prevents stale completion of theme half and dialog clearing)
missingStates: ipc_abort (cancel in-flight wallpaper apply/remove when superseded)
userImpact: Rapid environment switches can cause wallpaper flickering - the old environment's wallpaper injection completes after the new one started, briefly showing the wrong wallpaper on the agent.

scenario: User opens the app and ThemeSeeder runs installAll() during boot to seed built-in themes. This iterates packages sequentially with no progress callback. If seeding 12+ themes takes several seconds, the boot progress UI has no granular visibility into this phase.
userImpact: Boot progress stalls at the seeding phase with no sub-step granularity. On slow disks or first-run with many themes, the user sees a static spinner and may think the app hung.

scenario: User successfully applies a theme with a bundled wallpaper (theme.wallpaper.workshopId). themeStore.applyToApp calls wallpaperStore.activateThemeWallpaper, which reloads the wallpaper list and checks if workshopId exists. If the user does not own that workshop wallpaper, the function silently no-ops - no wallpaper activates, no notification shown.
missingStates: wallpaper_not_owned_feedback (notify when theme wallpaper is not in user library)
userImpact: Theme apply succeeds but the expected dynamic wallpaper never appears. User gets no explanation that the wallpaper was skipped because it is not in their library.

scenario: User applies a theme to an agent. theme-apply-flow.ts fires background tasks (secondary inject, hardening, wallpaper inject, scheme sync) as non-blocking promises. If the user immediately restores the agent after apply returns but before the background wallpaper inject runs, the restore clears everything, then the background task injects wallpaper onto the now-native agent page - wallpaper flashes back after restore.
supportedStates: apply response (returns after core CSS inject + persist)
missingStates: background_task_cancellation_on_restore (abort hardening/wallpaper/scheme chain when restore supersedes)
userImpact: Apply followed immediately by restore causes wallpaper to flash back. The injected wallpaper from the apply background task survives the restore because the epoch guard only checks before injectAgentWallpaperFromApply - if it already started, it completes on a now-native agent page.

scenario: User runs Visual Analyzer EXPORT_THEME with a valid palette. The handler dynamically imports scripts/build-theme-package.mjs via pathToFileURL(app.getAppPath()). In a packaged Electron app, scripts/ is inside asar (read-only). The dynamic import of a .mjs from within asar may fail, causing EXPORT_THEME to return {ok:false} with no error detail.
missingStates: asar_path_verification (verify build-theme-package.mjs is accessible in packaged context)
userImpact: Export theme silently fails in production builds. Developer test passes (dynamic import resolves in dev), but packaged app cannot import the script. User gets ok:false with no diagnostic information.

scenario: User deletes a wallpaper that is currently assigned as a per-agent wallpaper. deleteWallpaper correctly clears the global selectedId, but does NOT clear agentWallpapers[appId] entries pointing to the deleted wallpaper. Agents still show enabled in settings but injection silently fails on next apply.
supportedStates: global selection cleanup (selectedId cleared on delete)
missingStates: per-agent cleanup (clear agentWallpapers entries pointing to deleted wallpaper)
userImpact: After deleting a wallpaper, agents that had it assigned still show enabled in settings but injection silently fails. User sees no indication that the wallpaper assignment is now stale.

scenario: User selects an alternative color scheme in the DetailPanel's ColorSchemePicker. The schemeId is stored in local useState and used when Apply is clicked. If the user switches schemes, navigates away (unmounts DetailPanel), and returns, the schemeId is lost (reset by the selection-change useEffect). The user must re-select their preferred scheme every time they view the theme.
supportedStates: scheme selection (local useState, reset on theme switch)
missingStates: scheme persistence across navigation (restore last-selected scheme per theme)
userImpact: User picks a scheme variant, navigates away and back, finds the scheme reset to default. Must re-select every time. A state lifecycle inconsistency that breaks the edit flow.
